data.content_ref: inline:The target's countercondition explicitly concedes that expert intuition may use pattern-matching cognitive architecture that can perceive global structures a checklist cannot decompose. Under that concession the claim's 'false dichotomy' framing collapses: if the expert's process can perceive features a checklist cannot represent, then the two are not merely different executions of the same feature search, and the panel's explicit checklist is not just a more transparent version of the same procedure. Yet the target offers no causal mechanism for why, in that pattern-matching case, the panel's literalist-error tendency would be prevented from degrading reliability, so it has not argued the panel would be more reliable. It also never engages the problem's required evidence test: it gives no within-evaluation diagnostic that separates a true reliability gain from checklist compliance tracking the right answer, which the problem explicitly demands.
